inchinare.author: Timothy Keller
inchinare.text: Only if your god can outrage and challenge you will you know that you worship the real God and not a figment of your imagination. . . . If your god never disagrees with you, you might just be worshiping an idealized version of yourself.

inchinare.author: Timothy Keller
inchinare.text: The glory of God is available to you in the church in a way it's not available to you anywhere else. . . . There is no more important means of discipleship than deep involvement in the life of the church.

inchinare.author: Timothy Keller
inchinare.text: When you come to Christ, you must drop your conditions. You have to give up the right to say, 'I will obey you if . . . I will do this if . . .' As soon as you say, 'I will obey you if,' that is not obedience at all. You are saying: 'You are my adviser, not my Lord. I will be happy to take your recommendations. And I might even do some of them.' No. If you want Jesus with you, you have to give up the right to self-determination. Self-denial is an act of rebellion against our late-modern culture of self-assertion. But that is what we are called to. Nothing less.

inchinare.author: Timothy Keller
inchinare.text: Traditional religion says, 'I give God a good moral record, so he has to bless me.' The gospel says, 'God gives me a good moral record through Christ, so I want to bless him.' . . . Religion says, 'If I obey, then God will love and accept me.' The gospel says, 'God loves and accepts me, therefore I want to obey.'

inchinare.author: Timothy Keller
inchinare.text: To say 'I know God forgives me, but I can't forgive myself' means you've failed an idol whose approval is more important than God's.

inchinare.author: Paul David Tripp
inchinare.text: The Sabbath is for us. It gives us regular times of rest without feeling guilty that we are not being productive. It calls us out of the distracting clamor of our daily lives into worship, reminding us that our identity, meaning, purpose, and hope are found in the Lord alone.

inchinare.author: Paul David Tripp
inchinare.text: The life of faith is about standing at the intersection of brokenness and longing, not questioning God's presence, power, or goodness, but continuing to trust and obey, assured that he still rules and is marching his world toward the fullness of all he has promised.

inchinare.author: Paul David Tripp
inchinare.text: An idol of the heart is anything other than God that you allow to rule your heart.

inchinare.author: Paul David Tripp
inchinare.text: When I root my identity in the eternal grace and love of God rather than in an ever-changing world, temporary situations, relationships, or achievements, I can live with peace and security of heart, no matter how my circumstances might change.

inchinare.author: John Piper
inchinare.text: God is most glorified in us when we are most satisfied in Him.

inchinare.author: John Piper
inchinare.text: Worship is a way of gladly reflecting back to God the radiance of His worth.

inchinare.author: John Piper
inchinare.text: We are all starved for the glory of God, not self. No one goes to the Grand Canyon to increase self-esteem. Why do we go? Because there is greater healing for the soul in beholding splendor than there is in beholding self.

inchinare.author: John Piper
inchinare.text: O, God of wonder, enlarge my capacity to be amazed at what is amazing, and end my attraction to the insignificant.

inchinare.author: John Piper
inchinare.text: The deepest longing of the human heart is to know and enjoy the glory of God. We were made for this.

inchinare.author: John Piper
inchinare.text: Our obedience is God's pleasure when it proves that God is our treasure.

inchinare.author: John Piper
inchinare.text: God created us for this: to live our lives in a way that makes him look more like the greatness and the beauty and the infinite worth that he really is. This is what it means to be created in the image of God.

inchinare.author: John Piper
inchinare.text: If you can't see the sun you will be impressed with a street light. If you've never felt thunder and lightning you'll be impressed with fireworks. And if you turn your back on the greatness and majesty of God you'll fall in love with a world of shadows and short-lived pleasures.

inchinare.author: John Piper
inchinare.text: It is about the greatness of God, not the significance of man. God made man small and the universe big to say something about himself.

inchinare.author: Richard Wurmbrand
inchinare.text: There was once a fiddler who played so beautifully that everybody danced. A deaf man who could not hear the music considered them all insane. Those who are with Jesus in suffering hear this music to which other men are deaf. They dance and do not care if they are considered insane.

inchinare.author: Richard Wurmbrand
inchinare.text: A man who visits a barber to be shaved, or who orders a suit from a tailor, is not a disciple, but a customer. So one who comes to the Savior only to be saved is the Savior's customer, not His disciple. A disciple is one who says to Christ, 'How I long to do work like Yours!'

inchinare.author: Richard Wurmbrand
inchinare.text: To believe in Him is not such a great thing. To become like Him is truly great.

inchinare.author: Richard Wurmbrand
inchinare.text: Not all of us are called to die a martyr's death, but all of us are called to have the same spirit of self-sacrifice and love to the very end as these martyrs had.

inchinare.author: Timothy Keller
inchinare.text: Only when our greatest love is God, a love that we cannot lose even in death, can we face all things with peace.

inchinare.author: Timothy Keller
inchinare.text: You will never really understand your heart when things are going well. It is only when things go badly that you can see it truly. And that's because it is only when suffering comes that you realize who is the true God and what are the false gods of your lives.

inchinare.author: Timothy Keller
inchinare.text: Only the true God can go with you through that furnace and out to the other side. The other gods will abandon you in the furnace.

rugaciune.author: Timothy Keller
rugaciune.text: The only person who dares wake up a king at 3:00 a.m. for a glass of water is a child. We have that kind of access.

rugaciune.author: Timothy Keller
rugaciune.text: It is hard to stay angry at someone if you are praying for them. It is also hard to stay angry unless you feel superior, and it is hard to feel superior if you are praying for them, since in prayer you approach God as a forgiven sinner.

rugaciune.author: Timothy Keller
rugaciune.text: Prayer is the only entryway into genuine self-knowledge. It is also the main way we experience deep change—the reordering of our loves. Prayer is how God gives us so many of the unimaginable things he has for us. Indeed, prayer makes it safe for God to give us many of the things we most desire. It is the way we know God, the way we finally treat God as God. Prayer is simply the key to everything we need to do and be in life.

rugaciune.author: Timothy Keller
rugaciune.text: God will either give us what we ask or give us what we would have asked if we knew everything he knows.

rugaciune.author: Timothy Keller
rugaciune.text: We know God will answer us when we call because one terrible day he did not answer Jesus when he called. . . . Jesus' prayers were given the rejection that we sinners merit so that our prayers could have the reception that he merits.

rugaciune.author: Paul David Tripp
rugaciune.text: The power of prayer is not in the beauty of my language or in my track record of righteousness, but in the character of the one to whom I pray.

rugaciune.author: Paul David Tripp
rugaciune.text: Prayer is not about bringing your list of wants or perceived needs to God and asking him to sign off. No, prayer is surrendering all your wants and desires to the perfect plan and will of your heavenly Father.

rugaciune.author: John Piper
rugaciune.text: Prayer is the open admission that without Christ we can do nothing. And prayer is the turning away from ourselves to God in the confidence that He will provide the help we need. Prayer humbles us as needy and exalts God as wealthy.

rugaciune.author: Richard Wurmbrand
rugaciune.text: Are you seeking Jesus? Where have you been looking for Him? As you begin your day, think through the various places you will be and the people you will be with; and envision Jesus standing next to you in each of those places.

rugaciune.author: Richard Wurmbrand
rugaciune.text: Did I believe in God? Now the test had come. I was alone. There was no salary to earn, no golden opinions to consider. God offered me only suffering—would I continue to love Him?

rugaciune.author: Timothy Keller
rugaciune.text: God is very patient with us when we are desperate. Pour out your soul to him.

rugaciune.author: Timothy Keller
rugaciune.text: To pray is to accept that we are, and always will be, wholly dependent on God for everything.

rugaciune.author: Timothy Keller
rugaciune.text: If we can't say 'thy will be done' from the bottom of our hearts, we will never know any peace.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: Contemporary people tend to examine the Bible, looking for things they can't accept; but Christians should reverse that, allowing the Bible to examine us, looking for things God can't accept.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: Satan doesn't control us with fang marks on the flesh but with lies in the heart. . . . Our best defense in the fight against [his] lies is not the production of incantations but the rehearsal of truth.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: The gospel is that I am so sinful that Jesus had to die for me, yet so loved and valued that Jesus was glad to die for me. This leads to deep humility and deep confidence at the same time. I can't feel superior to anyone, and yet I have nothing to prove to anyone.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: The doctrine of sin means believers are never as good as our true worldview should make us. And the doctrine of common grace means unbelievers are never as flawed as their false worldview should make them.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: The gospel says you are simultaneously more sinful and flawed than you ever dared believe, yet more loved and accepted than you ever dared hope.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: If you're falling off a cliff, strong faith in a weak branch is fatally inferior to weak faith in a strong branch. Salvation is not finally based on the strength of your faith, but on the object of your faith.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: If Jesus rose from the dead, then you have to accept all that he said. If he didn't, then why worry about any of what he said? The issue on which everything hangs is not whether you like his teaching, but whether he rose from the dead.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: The central basis of Christian assurance is not how much our hearts are set on God, but how unshakably his heart is set on us.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: All death can now do to Christians is to make their lives infinitely better.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: To be loved but not known is superficial. To be known but not loved is our nightmare. Only Jesus knows us to the bottom and loves us to the sky.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: The temptation for those who suffer is to assume that because we can't think of any good purposes God may have for our suffering, there can't be any.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: There are the good things of this world, the hard things of this world, and the best things of this world—God's love, glory, holiness, beauty. The Bible's teaching is that the road to the best things is not through the good things but usually through the hard things. . . . There is no message more contrary to the way the world understands life or more subversive to its values.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: When Jesus Christ was in the garden of Gethsemane and the ultimate darkness was coming down on him and he knew it was coming, he didn't abandon you; he died for you. If Jesus Christ didn't abandon you in his darkness, the ultimate darkness, why would he abandon you now, in yours?

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: Only a grasp of what Jesus did on the cross—the doctrine of substitutionary atonement—can prevent spiritual distortions. . . . Only this doctrine keeps us from thinking God is mainly holy with some love or mainly loving with some holiness—but instead [he] is both holy and loving equally, interdependently. Only this view of God makes the spoiled or the neglected into the healthy and the loved.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: True repentance begins where whitewashing ('Nothing really happened') and blame-shifting ('It wasn't really my fault') and self-pity ('I'm sorry because of what it has cost me') and self-flagellation ('I will feel so terrible no one will be able to criticize me') end.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: Forgiveness is granted (often a good while) before it is felt—not felt before it is granted. It is a promise to not exact the price of sin from the person who hurt you. . . . If you wait to feel it before you grant it, you'll never grant it; you'll be in an anger prison.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: The only storm that can really destroy—the storm of divine justice and judgment on sin and evil—will never come upon you. Jesus bowed his head into that ultimate storm, willingly, for you. He died, receiving the punishment for sin we deserve, so we can be pardoned when we trust in him. When you see him doing that for you, it certainly does not answer all the questions you have about your suffering. But it proves that, despite it all, he still loves you.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: If you want to understand your own behavior, you must understand that all sin against God is grounded in a refusal to believe that God is more dedicated to our good, and more aware of what that is, than we are.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: When you say, 'Doctrine doesn't matter; what matters is that you live a good life,' that is a doctrine. It is called the doctrine of salvation by your works rather than by grace.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: If the suffering Jesus endured did not make him give up on us, nothing will.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: Through faith in the cross we get a new foundation for an identity that both humbles us out of our egoism yet is so infallibly secure in love that we are enabled to embrace rather than exclude those who are different.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: A good sermon is not like a club that beats upon the will but like a sword that cuts to the heart.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: Expository preaching should provide the main diet of preaching for a Christian community. . . . [It] is the best method for displaying and conveying your conviction that the whole Bible is true. This approach testifies that you believe every part of the Bible to be God's Word, not just particular themes and not just the parts you feel comfortable agreeing with.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: Preaching is not only explaining the text but also using it to engage the heart. I often see preachers giving so much time to the first task that they put little thought and ingenuity into the second.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: Every time you expound a Bible text, you are not finished unless you demonstrate how it shows us that we cannot save ourselves and that only Jesus can.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: Christian communicators must show that we remember (or at least understand) very well what it is like not to believe.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: It's in death that God says, 'If I'm not your security, then you've got no security, because I'm the only thing that can't be taken away from you. I will hold you in my everlasting arms. Every other set of arms will fail you, but I will never fail you.'

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: Mercy isn't just the job of the Christian. Mercy is the mark of the Christian.

cuvant.author: Paul David Tripp
cuvant.text: Our hope in life and death rests on our Savior's faithfulness, not our own.

cuvant.author: Paul David Tripp
cuvant.text: In the darkness of the days we live in, do not panic. Our Lord is on his throne in power and glory, and he will win.

cuvant.author: Paul David Tripp
cuvant.text: Once God has chosen you as his own, you cannot outrun his grace.

cuvant.author: Paul David Tripp
cuvant.text: As a wise Father, God always knows what is best for his children. His plans are always best. His way is always right. We will never know more than he knows or be wiser than he is.

cuvant.author: Paul David Tripp
cuvant.text: You may not always see God's hand, but you can rest assured that your Lord never ceases working for your good and his glory.

cuvant.author: Paul David Tripp
cuvant.text: The theology that you actually believe is always exhibited by the way you live. For too many of us, a disconcerting gap lies between what we say we believe and the way we live.

cuvant.author: Paul David Tripp
cuvant.text: You will walk through dark valleys, but your identity and future are secured by the fact that the steadfast love of the Lord endures forever.

cuvant.author: Paul David Tripp
cuvant.text: Although we face hardship, disappointment, and suffering, our lives are built on Jesus the sure foundation. We have a security that can never be shaken.

cuvant.author: Paul David Tripp
cuvant.text: If you forget or minimize the extent to which Jesus had to suffer in order to deal with your sin, then you will forget or minimize the gravity of your sin.

cuvant.author: Paul David Tripp
cuvant.text: God will crush evil and restore and purify his people. Evil will not win. Renewal is on the way. There's reason for hope.

cuvant.author: Paul David Tripp
cuvant.text: It is important to remember that God's grace never calls wrong right. Grace reminds us of sin's consequences and then offers us forgiveness and the power to say no.

cuvant.author: Paul David Tripp
cuvant.text: On the cross of Jesus Christ, God's anger with sin and his grace toward the sinner embrace. There we find everything we need to finally be what we were created to be and to live as God designed us to live.

cuvant.author: Paul David Tripp
cuvant.text: Hope is found in only one place: the power of our Lord to bring dry bones together again and breathe life into them. Our God has the power to bring life out of what is dead.

cuvant.author: Paul David Tripp
cuvant.text: As you look at broken things in your life, remember that your Lord is the Lord of fresh starts and new beginnings. Because of his grace, what seems irreparably damaged can be restored and live anew.

cuvant.author: Paul David Tripp
cuvant.text: God makes it clear in his word that, for our good and his glory, he will lead us through the unexpected, the unwanted, and the difficult.

cuvant.author: John Piper
cuvant.text: A Christian is not a person who believes in his head the teachings of the Bible. Satan believes in his head the teachings of the Bible! A Christian is a person who has died with Christ, whose stiff neck has been broken, whose brazen forehead has been shattered, whose stony heart has been crushed, whose pride has been slain, and whose life is now mastered by Jesus Christ.

cuvant.author: John Piper
cuvant.text: The wisdom of God devised a way for the love of God to deliver sinners from the wrath of God while not compromising the righteousness of God.

cuvant.author: John Piper
cuvant.text: Sin is what you do when your heart is not satisfied with God.

cuvant.author: John Piper
cuvant.text: One of the great enemies of hope is forgetting God's promises.

cuvant.author: John Piper
cuvant.text: Faith begins with a backward look at the cross, but it lives with a forward look at the promises.

cuvant.author: John Piper
cuvant.text: The key that unlocks the treasure chest of God's peace is faith in the promises of God.

cuvant.author: John Piper
cuvant.text: I know of no other way to triumph over sin long-term than to gain a distaste for it because of a superior satisfaction in God.

cuvant.author: John Piper
cuvant.text: The ultimate difference between God's wisdom and man's wisdom is how they relate to the glory of God's grace in Christ crucified. God's wisdom makes the glory of God's grace our supreme treasure. But man's wisdom delights in seeing himself as resourceful, self-sufficient, self-determining, and not utterly dependent on God's free grace.

cuvant.author: John Piper
cuvant.text: In EVERY situation and EVERY circumstance of your life, God is always doing a thousand different things that you cannot see and you do not know.

cuvant.author: John Piper
cuvant.text: What could be a greater privilege than to listen to the voice of God, and be granted by God himself the ears to hear?

cuvant.author: Richard Wurmbrand
cuvant.text: God will judge us not according to how much we endured, but how much we could love.

cuvant.author: Richard Wurmbrand
cuvant.text: He said there were two kinds of Christians: those who sincerely believe in God and those who, just as sincerely, believe that they believe. You can tell them apart by their actions in decisive moments.

cuvant.author: Richard Wurmbrand
cuvant.text: Even the best of Christians are troubled by the question, 'Why does an almighty God send, or at least allow, suffering?' When you are nagged by thoughts like this, say to yourself, 'I am still in elementary school. When I graduate from the university of Christian life, I will understand His ways better and doubts will cease.'

cuvant.author: Richard Wurmbrand
cuvant.text: I have found truly jubilant Christians only in the Bible, in the Underground Church and in prison.

cuvant.author: Richard Wurmbrand
cuvant.text: I found that joy can be acquired like a habit, in the same way as a folded sheet of paper falls naturally into the same fold.

cuvant.author: Richard Wurmbrand
cuvant.text: God chooses people whom the world does not hold in high esteem—simple souls who have stumbled, and who in their ignorance have become a prey to wickedness.

cuvant.author: Richard Wurmbrand
cuvant.text: From now on a fire burned within us, as it did in the disciples on the road to Emmaus. 'Snowflakes cannot fall on a hot stove,' says an Indian proverb. The coldness of this world could no longer harm us, although we had to pass through bitter times.

cuvant.author: Richard Wurmbrand
cuvant.text: Persecution has always produced a better Christian—a witnessing Christian, a soul-winning Christian. Communist persecution has backfired and produced serious, dedicated Christians such as are rarely seen in free lands.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: Any person who only sticks with Christianity as long as things are going his or her way, is a stranger to the cross.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: Everything in this life is going to be taken away from us, except one thing: God's love, which can go into death with us and take us through it and into His arms.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: Just because you can't see or imagine a good reason why God would allow something bad to happen doesn't mean there can't be one.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: Jesus was patient under even greater suffering for us, so that we can be patient under lesser suffering for him.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: Christ's miracles were not the suspension of the natural order but the restoration of the natural order. They were a reminder of what once was prior to the fall and a preview of what will eventually be a universal reality once again—a world of peace and justice, without death, disease, or conflict.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: So suffering is at the very heart of the Christian faith. It is not only the way Christ became like and redeemed us, but it is one of the main ways we become like him and experience his redemption.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: The only love that won't disappoint you is one that can't change, that can't be lost, that is not based on the ups and downs of life or of how well you live. It is something that not even death can take away from you. God's love is the only thing like that.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: While other worldviews lead us to sit in the midst of life's joys, foreseeing the coming sorrows, Christianity empowers its people to sit in the midst of this life's sorrows, tasting the coming joy.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: Christ's resurrection not only gives you hope for the future; it gives you hope to handle your scars right now.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: Suffering is the stripping of our hope in finite things, therefore we do not put our ultimate hope in anything finite.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: Human beings are hope-shaped creatures. The way you live now is completely controlled by what you believe about your future.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: The glory of the Christian life is that we have a hope that overwhelms grief. It doesn't eradicate it. It sweetens it. It overwhelms it.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: Only an imperishable hope can satisfy the human heart.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: But resurrection is not just consolation — it's restoration.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: Christians see hard things as indeed hard and not to be sought, but we have been armed with this great truth, namely that when received with faith in God, hard things lead to the best things.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: The resurrection of Christ promises us not merely some future consolation for the life we lost but the restoration of the life we lost and infinitely more. It promises the world and life that we have always longed for but never had.

cuvant.author: Timothy Keller
cuvant.text: Death was not part of God's original design. We were not created to age, weaken, fade, and die. We were not created for love relationships that end in death. Our sense even now that we were made to last, that we were made for love without parting, is a memory trace of our divine origins.

work.author: Timothy Keller
work.text: If you make work your identity and you succeed, it'll go to your head. If you fail, it'll go to your heart.

work.author: Paul David Tripp
work.text: Joy in labor is possible only when you are thankful that God has provided you with a job and the ability to work.

work.author: Paul David Tripp
work.text: Contentment depends not on your situation but on the heart that you bring to each situation.

work.author: Paul David Tripp
work.text: In his greatness, God has more than enough power to meet you in your weakness and to empower you to be what he has redeemed you to be and to do what he has redeemed you to do.

work.author: John Piper
work.text: Life is precarious, and life is precious. Don't presume you will have it tomorrow, and don't waste it today.

work.author: John Piper
work.text: But whatever you do, find the God-centered, Christ-exalting, Bible-saturated passion of your life, and find your way to say it and live for it and die for it. And you will make a difference that lasts. You will not waste your life.

work.author: John Piper
work.text: God created us to live with a single passion: to joyfully display his supreme excellence in all spheres of life. The wasted life is the life without this passion. God calls us to pray and think and dream and plan and work, not to be made much of, but to make much of him in every part of our lives.
